# python3-pyhamtools

**Python library for callsign lookup, locators and DXCC data**

- **Version recorded:** 0.11.0
- **Categories:** `logging`, `references`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/dh1tw/pyhamtools>

## What it does

A library, not a program. It resolves a callsign to its DXCC entity, CQ and ITU zone and continent using country files or online sources, converts between Maidenhead locators and coordinates, computes distance and bearing between two points, and looks up callsigns against QRZ, HamQTH and ClubLog.

## Why you would want it

Every one of those is a small job that is easy to get subtly wrong -- DXCC entity resolution in particular is a table of exceptions, not a rule. If you are writing anything that touches callsigns, this is the difference between a script that works and a script that works except for the interesting prefixes.

## Before it will work

Python 3. Online lookups need network access and, for QRZ, an account; offline entity resolution works from a country file with no network at all.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profiles:** [`logging`](../profiles/logging.md), [`propagation`](../profiles/propagation.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install python3-pyhamtools --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `python3-pyhamtools`

## Known problems

Country files age. DXCC entities are added, deleted and redefined, and a stale cty.dat resolves a new prefix to the wrong entity silently -- the library reports an answer, not a doubt. Refresh the data rather than trusting a cached copy for award-critical work.
